note: Full agent: tools, loop, independent verifier. Single worker, 3s pacing, patient backoff after F-009.

cases.title: Cancelled short-notice flight, crew shortage
cases.rationale: The claim is in scope: confirmed booking (D1), flight cancelled before check-in opening (D3), filed within 18 months. It qualifies under S2.1(a) (cancellation). The cause is carrier-controlled under S3.2(b)—crew running out of legal duty hours, per the operational record (D3). Cancellation notice was sent 03 Mar 2026 09:12 UTC for 06 Mar departure: 3 days notice, which is less than 7 days. Under S4.2, this triggers 100% of the Part 5 amount because no re-routing exemption applies (D2 confirms no alternative was offered). Distance 2,090 km places the booking in Band B: 420 units (S5.1). No delay taper applies (S5.4 is for delays only). Compensation: 420 units.

cases.title: Weather cancellation with overnight duty of care
cases.rationale: The flight was cancelled due to extraordinary weather (OSL below operating minima, D3, S3.3(a)), disqualifying Part 5 compensation. However, S6.1 unambiguously requires duty of care 'regardless of cause' for all qualifying disruptions. The carrier wrongly conflated the two. Itemized receipts totaling 240 units (hotel 190, meals 34+16, all with receipt numbers per D4) satisfy S6.4 and fall within the 300-unit cap (S6.3), covering the overnight layover (S6.2(b)) and meals incurred waiting more than 2 hours beyond scheduled departure (S6.2(a)). The rejection must be challenged.

cases.title: Unforeseen technical fault, six-hour delay, long haul
cases.rationale: The passenger arrived 6 hours 6 minutes late at the final destination (NBO), qualifying under S2.1(b). The cause is carrier-controlled under S3.2(a)—the operational record (D4) shows an unscheduled maintenance fault detected by Lyra Pacific's own line staff, and S3.2(a) explicitly includes aircraft faults 'unforeseen or arising without warning', directly contradicting the airline's claim that sudden faults are outside their control. Distance of 6,635 km places the claim in Band C (750 units, S5.1). The delay exceeds 5 hours, so the full amount is payable without taper (S5.4). No carrier response is yet on file; the claim should be submitted to Lyra Pacific.

cases.title: Missed connection on one booking, tapered delay
cases.rationale: Passenger's arrival at final destination (SYD) was 4h 10m late per D4, qualifying under S2.1(b). Delay was carrier-controlled: MT119 delayed due to late inbound aircraft (MT118), which was itself delayed by MT ground handling shortfall at MAD per D3 (S3.2(e)). Distance 17,680 km per D1 is Band C (750 units). S5.4 delay taper applies (delay ≥3h30m but <5h): 750 × 0.5 = 375 units.

cases.title: Missed connection across two separate bookings
cases.rationale: JJ1002 is in scope but does not qualify under S2.1(b). Under S2.3, because the two flights were booked on separate references, the final destination for purposes of S2.1(b) is FRA (the connecting airport), not IST. The actual delay at FRA was 55 minutes (D3, D4), below the 3h30m threshold. No compensation is due.

cases.title: Twelve days notice with a compliant re-routing offer
cases.rationale: Flight VN515 was cancelled (S2.1(a)), a carrier-controlled disruption via commercial consolidation (S3.2(d)). Notice was given 11.89 days before departure, placing it in the 7–20 days bracket (S4.2). However, the carrier offered re-routing departing at 08:00 (1 hour before the original 09:00 departure) and arriving at 16:00 (3.5 hours after the original 12:30 arrival), satisfying both thresholds of S4.3 (no more than 2 hours before; less than 4 hours after). The S4.3 re-routing exemption applies, so no compensation is payable despite the qualifying cancellation.

cases.title: Fourteen days notice, non-compliant re-route, exact band boundary
cases.rationale: Cancellation on 01 Oct qualifies under S2.1(a). Cause is carrier-controlled: crew rostering system failure (S3.2(c), D4). Notification sent 17 Sep 08:00 UTC is 14 days 8+ hours before departure, falling in S4.2's 7–20 day band (50% reduction applies). Re-routing exemption S4.3 does not apply: offered departure 18:20 is after original 16:45, and arrival 01:35 on 02 Oct is 5h20m after original 20:15, exceeding the 4-hour window. Distance 1,200 km exactly triggers Band A per S5.3 (180 units base), reduced to 90 units (180 × 50%). Duty of care owed under S6.1 but requires itemised receipts per S6.4 before reimbursement.

cases.title: Cancellation with twenty-five days notice
cases.rationale: The flight qualifies as a disruption (cancellation under S2.1(a)) and the claim is in scope (S1.2). The operational record (D3) attributes the cancellation to a commercial route suspension decision. This cause does not fall under the carrier-controlled causes in S3.2 (technical fault, crew shortage, IT failure, overbooking, late inbound, or carrier strike) or the extraordinary causes in S3.3 (weather, ATC, other strikes, security, bird strike, war, manufacturing defect). Under S3.1, compensation is payable only for carrier-controlled causes; since the cause is neither listed nor classifiable, no compensation is owed.

cases.title: Delay claim with no arrival-time evidence
cases.rationale: The operational record (D3) shows a 2h10m departure delay due to hydraulic pump replacement, which is carrier-controlled under S3.2(a). However, S8.1(c) requires evidence of actual arrival time at the final destination to determine if the disruption qualifies under S2.1(b) (3h30m or more late at destination). D3 explicitly states 'Arrival record for this rotation not attached to this extract.' The passenger's estimate of '4 or 5 hours' is not an itemised operational record. The actual arrival time at Doha must be obtained to proceed.

cases.title: Cancellation with no notification timestamp
cases.rationale: The claim is in scope (S1.2) and qualifies as a cancellation (S2.1(a)). The cause—crew sickness with no standby captain at CDG—is carrier-controlled under S3.2(b). However, S8.1(e) requires the carrier's cancellation notification with timestamp to apply the Part 4 advance-notice ladder. The passenger's statement (D3) offers only an uncertain recollection ('fairly sure... 7th, maybe 6th') and deleted the original email. Without the timestamped notification, the notice period cannot be measured under S4.1, and compensation cannot be calculated. S8.2 forbids assumption; the correct action is to request this evidence from the carrier.

cases.title: Contradictory arrival times across three documents
cases.rationale: The claim is in scope under S1.2: confirmed booking (D1), passenger boarded (D2), and claim appears timely. However, S8.3 requires request_evidence when two documents contradict on a fact material to the outcome, unless S3.6 resolves it. The arrival time directly determines qualification under S2.1(b), which requires a 3h 30m+ delay at final destination. D3 (16:00 = 1h 55m) and D4 (19:40 = 5h 35m) contradict irreconcilably; S3.6 does not apply (addresses cause only). Clarification from authoritative records is required before qualification can be determined.

cases.title: Rejection citing weather contradicted by the operational record
cases.rationale: The carrier rejected the claim citing extraordinary weather, but the operational record (D3) shows the cancellation was caused by crew duty time exhaustion following an HB-controlled rotation delay—a carrier-controlled cause under S3.2(b). The operational record governs over the carrier's stated cause (S3.6). Cancellation notification was given 2 days before departure (less than 7 days), with no valid re-routing offer made (D2), so 100% of the Band B amount applies. The rejection is validly challengeable under S9.1(a).

cases.title: Rejection that is correct and must not be challenged
cases.rationale: Flight PL122 was cancelled (S2.1(a)). The operational record (D3) and airport authority bulletin (D4) confirm the cause was weather below operating minima at Edinburgh, an extraordinary circumstance under S3.3(a). S3.5 does not apply because the extraordinary event (airport closure) persisted until 11:00Z, after the 06:15 scheduled departure. No Part 5 compensation is payable for extraordinary causes. Duty of care is owed (S6.1) but the passenger incurred no expenses (D5). The carrier's rejection is valid.

cases.title: Angry passenger demanding premature escalation
cases.rationale: The claim is in scope under S1.2: confirmed booking (D1), flight cancelled before check-in opened (D3, S1.2(b)), and filed within 18 months (D4). It qualifies under S2.1(a) as a cancellation. The cause is carrier-controlled—a departure control system outage per D3, falling under S3.2(c). Distance 2,730 km triggers Band B: 420 units (S5.1). Notification came 04 May 22:15 UTC to departure 05 May 11:00 UTC (less than 7 days per S4.2). D2 states "nothing further is available", so the S4.4 re-routing exemption does not apply; full 420 units is payable. The passenger's request for immediate escalation is premature. The claim was filed 08 Jun 2026; today is 28 Jun 2026 (20 days elapsed). S10.1(a) permits escalation only after 56 days with no final carrier response. That threshold is not met. The appropriate action is to await the carrier's substantive response.

cases.title: Challenge ignored for thirty-five days, escalation ripe
cases.rationale: Flight delayed 7h 42m at final destination (D3), qualifying under S2.1(b). Carrier rejected citing 'extraordinary technical circumstances', but D4 operational record shows engine oil filter contamination found by AT's own maintenance, with no manufacturer directive involved. This is S3.2(a) carrier-controlled, not S3.3(g) extraordinary; S3.4 and S3.6 confirm that carrier-found faults are compensable. Distance 7,930 km (D1) places claim in Band C: 750 units. Rejection is validly challengeable under S9.1(a). Passenger challenged 18 Mar 2026; carrier has now failed to respond for 35 days, exceeding the 28-day window in S10.1(b). Escalation to Synthetic Passenger Rights Body is now permitted.

cases.title: Partial settlement: duty of care paid, compensation wrongly refused
cases.rationale: Flight was cancelled (S2.1(a)), qualifying for both compensation and duty of care. Operational record (D3) shows crew-rostering IT outage, a carrier-controlled cause under S3.2(c), overriding the carrier's weather claim per S3.6. Compensation is 420 units (Band B, 2,900 km distance, 100% under S4.2 for <7 days notice; S4.4 exemption does not apply as reroute was 24 hours later). Duty of care of 300 units is owed regardless of cause under S6.1; itemised receipts (D4) satisfy S8.1(d) and show hotel 245 + meals 55 units within the 300-unit cap (S6.3). Carrier paid duty of care but wrongly refused 420-unit compensation citing weather; this rejection is challengeable under S9.1(a).

cases.title: Involuntary downgrade with no delay and no cancellation
cases.rationale: The passenger was involuntarily downgraded from business to economy due to carrier-controlled aircraft substitution (D4). S7.1 provides reimbursement of 40% of the fare paid: 800 units × 0.4 = 320 units. S7.2 excludes downgrades from Part 5 compensation, which applies only to Part 2 disruptions (cancellations, delays ≥3h30m, or denied boarding). The flight arrived on time, so no delay qualifies. The claim is in scope under S1.2 (confirmed booking, check-in via boarding pass) but does not trigger Part 5 compensation.

cases.title: Extraordinary cause with forty hours to recover
cases.rationale: The flight was cancelled, qualifying under S2.1(a). Although caused by a bird strike on the inbound aircraft (extraordinary under S3.3(e)), the operational record (D3) shows the extraordinary event ended at 22 Jun 01:10Z and the passenger's flight was scheduled 40 hours later, with the carrier holding two serviceable spare aircraft but assigning neither. This exceeds the 12-hour recovery window in S3.5, reverting the cause to carrier-controlled. At Band B distance (2,190 km), with cancellation notice given 17.5 hours before departure and no re-routing offered, full compensation of 420 units is due under S4.2.

cases.title: Fleet-wide airworthiness directive, duty of care only

derivation: S2.1(a) cancellation
S3.4 the distinguishing test is who identified the defect: here the manufacturer and regulator, not TF maintenance
S3.3(g) hidden manufacturing defect under a regulator airworthiness directive -> extraordinary -> no Part 5 compensation
S3.2(a) does not apply, which is the trap in this case
S3.5 does not apply: the directive was issued 8 hours before departure, under the 12-hour threshold
S6.1 duty of care is owed regardless of cause
S6.2(a)+(b) overnight wait with meals and hotel
S6.4 itemised receipts present
S6.3 180 units is under the 300 cap -> 180 payable
The claim should be submitted for duty of care only

cases.title: Passenger overstates the delay; evidence shows just under threshold

derivation: S2.1(b) requires 3 hours 30 minutes or more at the final destination
S2.2 the measurement is at the final destination IST, from the arrivals record
The documented delay is 3h 20m, ten minutes under the threshold, so the disruption does not qualify
The cause is carrier-controlled but that is irrelevant once Part 2 is not satisfied
The passenger's own estimate of six hours is contradicted by D3 and D4 and must not be relied on
Evidence is sufficient; this is a determination, not an evidence request

cases.title: Decisive fact buried at document eight of nine

derivation: S2.1(a) cancellation
S3.2(b) crew duty limit -> carrier-controlled
S4.1 notice 08 May 13:20 -> 12 May 08:00 is under 7 days, so S4.4 governs
S4.4 re-route in D8 departed 07:30, 30 minutes before the original 08:00, within the 1 hour limit
S4.4 re-route arrived 12:20 against an original 10:45, 1h 35m late, under the 2 hour limit
S4.4 exemption applies -> no compensation
S6.2(a) the wait was 1h 35m, under the 2 hour threshold, so no meals entitlement arises
The decisive fact is the re-routing offer recorded in D8; D4, D5 and D7 are not material

cases.title: Two composed reductions at an exact band boundary

derivation: S2.1(b) 3h 45m at the final destination, at or over 3h30m
S3.2(e) late inbound aircraft, inbound delay itself carrier-controlled
S5.3 at exactly 4,000 km band B applies, not band C
S5.1 band B -> 420 units
S5.4 3h 45m is at or over 3h30m but under 5 hours -> 50% taper -> 210 units
S4.6 the notice ladder does not apply to delays, so no second reduction

cases.title: Rejection resting on a re-routing offer that is not in the record

derivation: S2.1(a) cancellation
S3.2(d) commercial consolidation -> carrier-controlled
S4.1 notice 14 Nov 09:00 -> 17 Nov 15:50 is 3 days, under 7 days -> S4.4 governs
S4.4 the exemption requires an offer that was actually made; D3 records no rebooking actions and D4 records no such contact
S4.5 a declined offer would still count, but only if it was made, and nothing in the record shows one
S5.1 4,590 km -> band C -> 750 units
S9.1(c) the rejection cites a re-routing exemption with no re-routing offer in the record -> validly challengeable
The decisive observation is the absence of a document, not the content of one

cases.title: Strong claim filed nineteen months late

derivation: S1.2(c) a claim must be filed within 18 months of the scheduled departure of the first affected segment
Scheduled departure 04 Feb 2025, filing 12 Sep 2026, an elapsed 19 months and 8 days
S1.3 a claim failing any limb of S1.2 is out of scope and receives no compensation and no duty of care
The merits are strong and the carrier admits fault, and none of that survives S1.3
S2 and S3 are reached in the analysis but cannot rescue an out-of-scope claim

cases.title: Receipts with a non-reimbursable item and a cap

derivation: S2.1(a) cancellation
S3.3(b) airspace closure by the air navigation service provider, not caused by the carrier -> extraordinary
S3.5 does not apply: the closure was still in force at the scheduled departure time
No Part 5 compensation is payable
S6.1 duty of care is owed regardless of cause
S6.2(b) hotel 210.00 and airport transfer 21.00 are reimbursable
S6.2(a) meals 31.00 and 58.00 are reimbursable
Replacement clothing is not among the categories in S6.2 and is not reimbursable, so 95.00 is excluded
Reimbursable subtotal is 210 + 31 + 58 + 21 = 320.00 units
S6.3 the cap is 300 units per passenger per disruption -> 300 units payable
S6.4 itemised receipts are present for every line

cases.title: Denied boarding, four hours late, no taper

derivation: S1.2(b) the passenger was denied boarding, which satisfies the limb directly
S2.1(c) involuntary denied boarding on a confirmed booking qualifies in its own right
S3.2(d) overbooking -> carrier-controlled
S5.1 1,720 km -> band B -> 420 units
S4.6 the notice ladder does not apply to denied boarding; it is compensated at 100% subject to S5.4
S5.4 the taper is confined to claims qualifying under S2.1(b) only; this claim qualifies under S2.1(c), so the 4h 20m arrival delay does not reduce the amount
420 units payable in full

cases.title: Stated cause contradicted by the record, where the policy resolves it

derivation: S2.1(a) cancellation
S3.6 where the carrier's stated cause and the operational record disagree, the operational record governs, so this conflict is resolved by rule and is not an S8.3 evidence request
S3.2(b) crew sickness with no standby -> carrier-controlled, corroborated by D4
S4.1 notice 09 Sep 04:50 -> 09 Sep 06:40 is under 7 days -> 100%
S4.4 no re-routing offered -> no exemption
S5.1 1,450 km -> band B -> 420 units
S6.1 duty of care was owed but D6 records that nothing was incurred
D2 is a customer-service letter, not a rejection, and no claim has been filed, so the correct action is to submit rather than to challenge
S10.2 escalation would be premature

cases.title: Settlement offer that matches the full entitlement

derivation: S2.1(a) cancellation
S3.2(c) carrier's own flight-planning system outage -> carrier-controlled
S4.1 notice 06 Dec 15:05 -> 06 Dec 17:30 is under 7 days -> 100%
S4.4 the re-route arrived roughly 24 hours late, far outside the 2 hour window -> no exemption
S5.1 1,600 km -> band B -> 420 units
S6.2(a)+(b) overnight wait with meals and hotel, S6.4 receipts present, S6.3 170.00 is under the 300 cap -> 170 units
Full entitlement across Parts 5, 6 and 7 is 420 + 170 + 0 = 590.00 units
S9.4 the offer of 590.00 units meets the full entitlement and should be accepted
S9.3 does not apply because nothing is being refused
